analysis.investment_thesis: Devyani operates premium QSR brands (KFC, Pizza Hut) that benefit from India's aspirational consumption boom, but the financial reality is harsh: the company is loss-making with D/E of 1.71, Forward P/E of 127x, and rising finance costs of INR 267 Cr annually consuming cash generated from operations. The India QSR story is compelling but not at this price and this balance sheet.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 61.37% with RJ Corp backing — alignment is there; promoter has 35+ year track record in beverages/QSR
Revenue CAGR of 19.3% over 9 years is genuinely impressive, and OCF is positive and growing (INR 900 Cr in FY25) — restaurant-level economics work
Brand strength of KFC and Pizza Hut in India's underpenetrated QSR market with large store rollout potential in Tier 2/3 cities
key_risks: Chronically loss-making: Net Profit negative in 7 of last 10 years; FY24 -INR 10 Cr, FY25 -INR 7 Cr despite INR 4,951 Cr revenue — the business cannot convert sales into profits
Debt has exploded: Borrowings went from INR 1,565 Cr (FY23) to INR 3,343 Cr (FY25) with D/E of 1.71; finance costs of INR 267 Cr are strangling the P&L
Forward P/E of 127.2x for a loss-making, highly leveraged business is pricing in a turnaround that hasn't happened in 10 years of trying
red_flags: D/E of 1.71 is unacceptable for a restaurant company — real estate-heavy expansion is being funded entirely by debt, creating fragility in an economic slowdown
ROCE of only 6.42% — the company is deploying capital at returns below the cost of debt, destroying shareholder value with each new store opened on borrowed money

Persistent negative net profit despite strong OCF means lease/depreciation costs from aggressive store rollout are permanently impaired — the EBITDA story masks a poor unit economics reality at the PAT level
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Devyani presents the classic India QSR paradox — great brands, real consumption tailwind, but a capital allocation disaster. Revenue has grown from INR 1,012 Cr (FY16) to INR 4,951 Cr (FY25), yet the company has lost money in 7 of those 10 years. Each new store requires capex (INR 491 Cr in FY25) funded by debt, and the lease liabilities pile up in the balance sheet (total assets grew from INR 1,884 Cr to INR 6,207 Cr in 5 years, driven by lease capitalization under Ind AS 116).

I look at the numbers and see a business where OCF of INR 900 Cr is entirely consumed by capex (INR 491 Cr) and debt servicing (INR 267 Cr finance costs). The promoter is strong but the financial engineering through debt-funded expansion is concerning. India will absolutely consume more KFC and Pizza Hut, but Jubilant FoodWorks (Domino's) proves the same thesis with far better unit economics and no leverage. At 127x forward P/E for a loss-making, D/E 1.71 company, this is purely hope-priced. Avoid until deleveraging and sustained PAT profitability are demonstrated.
